He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV Runnin' Rebels]], where he was Co-Defensive Player of the Year as a senior. He was selected with the 13th pick in the first round of the [[2003 NBA draft]] by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], then traded to the [[Boston Celtics]], along with [[Kendrick Perkins]]. ==College career== After playing two years at [[Utah Tech University|Dixie College]], a junior college in [[St. George, Utah]], Banks transferred to [[UNLV]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/marcus_banks/bio.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071007102129/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/marcus_banks/bio.html|url-status=dead|title=Marcus Banks NBA.com bio.|website=[[NBA.com]] |archivedate=October 7, 2007}} He played for the [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV Runnin' Rebels]], where he was Co-Defensive Player of the Year of the [[Mountain West Conference]] as a senior. ==Professional career== ===NBA=== Banks was selected as the thirteenth pick in the first round of the [[2003 NBA draft]] by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]; however, he was then traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] along with [[Kendrick Perkins]] for [[Troy Bell]] and [[Dahntay Jones]]. The Celtics agreed to trade him to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2004 for [[Gary Payton]], but returned to Boston after the trade was amended following Payton's refusal to take a physical. Payton would later be acquired by the Celtics in a trade involving different players. In Boston, Banks was known for his good defense and ball handling; [[Allen Iverson]], a division-rival point guard, named Banks as the toughest defender he faced in his career.{{Cite tweet |author=Allen Iverson |user=Sixers |number=588489919288516608 |date=April 15, 2015 |title=Marcus Banks. #AskTheAnswer |access-date=April 16, 2015 }} However, coach [[Doc Rivers]] had high hopes for young guard [[Delonte West]], and Banks' minutes were reduced. On January 26, 2006, it was announced that Banks, [[Mark Blount]], [[Ricky Davis]] and [[Justin Reed]] were traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for [[Wally Szczerbiak]], [[Michael Olowokandi]] and [[Dwayne Jones (basketball player)|Dwayne Jones]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2307791 Szczerbiak, Davis change teams in seven-player trade.], Updated January 27, 2006 Banks signed as a [[free agent]] with the [[Phoenix Suns]] on July 19, 2006.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2524053|title=Report: Suns, point guard Banks agree to five-year deal|date=July 19, 2006|website=ESPN.com}} In 2007, the Suns spent training camp working Banks into a shooting-guard role when they were not seeking a trade, a tough proposition with Banks in the second year of a five-year, $21.3 million contract. On February 6, 2008, Banks, along with All-Star forward [[Shawn Marion]], was traded to the [[Miami Heat]] for [[Shaquille O'Neal]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3234099|title=Suns turn up Heat, getting Shaq for Marion, Banks|date=February 6, 2008|website=ESPN.com}} On February 13, 2009, Banks and Marion were traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] for [[Jermaine O'Neal]] and [[Jamario Moon]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/pressrelease_marion_021309.html|title=Raptors Acquire Marion And Banks From Miami|website=www.nba.com}} Banks' final game in the NBA was during his time with the Raptors on November 16, 2010, in a 94–109 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]]. In his final game, Banks recorded 2 points and 2 assists. On November 20, 2010, Banks was traded to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] with [[Jarrett Jack]] and [[David Andersen]] for [[Peja Stojaković]] and [[Jerryd Bayless]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_acquire_jack_anderson_2010_11_20.html |title=HORNETS ACQUIRE JACK, ANDERSON AND BANKS FROM RAPTORS. |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2010-11-20 |access-date=2010-11-21}} In his {{frac|5|1|2}}-month tenure with the Hornets, Banks never played a game for the team, effectively ending his NBA career.{{Cite
